l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Hercules is son of Jupiter
q: Hercules (in Greek, Heracles) was the son of Jupiter and Alemena.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Hercules slaughters Nemean lion (by strangling it)
q: After using in vain his club and arrows against the lion, Hercules strangled the animal with his hands.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: twelve Labors of Hercules includes Hydra (as a labor)
q: His next labor was to slaughter the Hydra.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Hydra ravages Argos
q: This monster ravaged the country of Argos, and dwelt in a swamp near the well of Amymone, of which the story is that when the country was suffering from drought, Neptune, who loved her, had permitted her to touch the rock with his trident, and a spring of three outlets burst forth.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Hydra has heads nine (one middle head is immortal)
q: The Hydra had nine heads, of which the middle one was immortal.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Iolaus assists Hercules (in destroying the Hydra)
q: At length with the assistance of his faithful servant Iolaus, he burned away the heads of the Hydra, and buried the ninth or immortal one under a huge rock.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: twelve Labors of Hercules includes Augean stables (as a labor)
q: Another labor was the cleaning of the Augean stables.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Augeas owns Augean stables (as king of Elis)
q: Augeas, king of Elis, had a herd of three thousand oxen, whose stalls had not been cleansed for thirty years.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Hercules cleanses Augean stables (by diverting the Alpheus and Peneus through them in one day)
q: Hercules brought the rivers Alpheus and Peneus through them, and cleansed them thoroughly in one day.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Amazons is a nation of women (warlike)
q: The Amazons were a nation of women. They were very warlike and held several flourishing cities.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Hippolyta is queen of Amazons
q: Hippolyta, the queen, received him kindly, and consented to yield him her girdle;

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Hercules is son of Jupiter
q: Hercules (in Greek, Heracles) was the son of Jupiter and Alemena.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Hippolyta possesses girdle of Hippolyta
q: Hippolyta, the queen, received him kindly, and consented to yield him her girdle;

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Hercules obtains girdle of Hippolyta (after Hippolyta's death)
q: Hercules, thinking that Hippolyta had acted treacherously, slew her, and taking her girdle, made sail homewards.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Geryon is a monster (with three bodies)
q: Geryon, a monster with three bodies who dwelt in the island Erytheia (the red), so called because it lay at the west, under the rays of the setting sun.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Geryon is king of Spain (according to the description's interpretation)
q: This description is thought to apply to Spain, of which Geryon was said to be king.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Pillars of Hercules consist of Calpe (one of the two mountains)
q: Hercules reached at length the frontiers of Libya and Europe, where he raised the two mountains of Calpe and Abyla, as monuments of his progress, or according to another account rent one mountain into two and left half on each side, forming the Straits of Gibraltar, the two mountains being called the Pillars of Hercules.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Pillars of Hercules consist of Abyla (one of the two mountains)
q: Hercules reached at length the frontiers of Libya and Europe, where he raised the two mountains of Calpe and Abyla, as monuments of his progress, or according to another account rent one mountain into two and left half on each side, forming the Straits of Gibraltar, the two mountains being called the Pillars of Hercules.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Pillars of Hercules form Straits of Gibraltar (according to another account)
q: Hercules reached at length the frontiers of Libya and Europe, where he raised the two mountains of Calpe and Abyla, as monuments of his progress, or according to another account rent one mountain into two and left half on each side, forming the Straits of Gibraltar, the two mountains being called the Pillars of Hercules.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: golden apples of the Hesperides is kept by Hesperides (with the assistance of a dragon)
q: These were the apples which Juno had received at her wedding from the goddess of the Earth, and which she had intrusted to the keeping of the daughters of Hesperis, assisted by a watchful dragon.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Hesperides is daughter of Hesperis
q: These were the apples which Juno had received at her wedding from the goddess of the Earth, and which she had intrusted to the keeping of the daughters of Hesperis, assisted by a watchful dragon.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Atlas is a Titan (defeated in the war against the gods)
q: Atlas was one of the Titans who had warred against the gods, and after they were subdued, Atlas was condemned to bear on his shoulders the weight of the heavens.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Hercules is son of Alcmene
q: Hercules (in Greek, Heracles) was the son of Jupiter and Alemena.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Atlas bears heavens (on his shoulders)
q: Atlas was one of the Titans who had warred against the gods, and after they were subdued, Atlas was condemned to bear on his shoulders the weight of the heavens.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Atlas is father of Hesperides
q: He was the father of the Hesperides, and Hercules thought, might, if any one could, find the apples and bring them to him.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Hercules returns the apples (to Eurystheus)
q: He returned with them, and though somewhat reluctantly, took his burden upon his shoulders again, and let Hercules return with the apples to Eurystheus.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Antaeus is a giant and wrestler (whose strength depended on contact with Earth)
q: Antaeus, the son of Terra (the Earth) was a mighty giant and wrestler, whose strength was invincible so long as he remained in contact with his mother Earth.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Antaeus is son of Earth
q: Antaeus, the son of Terra (the Earth) was a mighty giant and wrestler, whose strength was invincible so long as he remained in contact with his mother Earth.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Hercules defeats Antaeus (by lifting him from the earth and strangling him in the air)
q: Hercules encountered him, and finding that it was of no avail to throw him, for he always rose with renewed strength from every fall, he lifted him up from the earth and strangled him in the air.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Cacus is a giant (inhabiting a cave on Mount Aventine)
q: Cacus was a huge giant, who inhabited a cave on Mount Aventine (one of the seven hills of Rome), and plundered the surrounding country.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Hercules kills Cacus
q: Cacus was slain by Hercules.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Cerberus is a monster (of the lower world)
q: Hercules descended into Hades, accompanied by Mercury and Minerva. He obtained permission from Pluto to carry Cerberus to the upper air, provided he could do it without the use of weapons; and in spite of the monster's struggling he seized him, held him fast, and carried him to Eurystheus, and afterwards brought him back again.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Hercules carries Cerberus (from Hades without weapons and later returns him)
q: He obtained permission from Pluto to carry Cerberus to the upper air, provided he could do it without the use of weapons; and in spite of the monster's struggling he seized him, held him fast, and carried him to Eurystheus, and afterwards brought him back again.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Hercules is cousin of Eurystheus
q: He was however by the arts of Juno rendered subject to his cousin Eurystheus and compelled to perform all his commands.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Hercules is slave of Omphale (for three years)
q: Hercules in a fit of madness killed his friend Iphitus and was condemned for this offence to become the slave of Queen Omphale for three years.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Hercules is married to Dejanira
q: When this service was ended he married Dejanira and lived in peace with her three years.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Nessus is a Centaur
q: Nessus attempted to run away with her, but Hercules heard her cries, and shot an arrow into the heart of Nessus. The dying Centaur told Dejanira to take a portion of his blood and keep it, as it might be used as a charm to preserve the love of her husband.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: blood of Nessus is a love charm (intended to preserve a husband's love)
q: The dying Centaur told Dejanira to take a portion of his blood and keep it, as it might be used as a charm to preserve the love of her husband.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: blood of Nessus poisons Hercules (when the robe becomes warm on his body)
q: Dejanira, thinking it a good opportunity to try her love-spell, steeped the garment in the blood of Nessus. We are to suppose she took care to wash out all traces of it, but the magic power remained, and as soon as the garment became warm on the body of Hercules, the poison penetrated into all his limbs and caused him the most intense agony.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Dejanira dies by suicide hanging herself
q: Dejanira on seeing what she had unwittingly done, hung herself.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Mount Oeta contains funeral pile (prepared for Hercules)
q: Hercules, prepared to die, ascended Mount OEta, where he built a funeral pile of trees, gave his bow and arrows to Philoctetes, and laid himself down on the pile, his head resting on his club, and his lion's skin spread over him.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Hercules is immortal immortal (what he derived from me)
q: Only his mother's share in him can perish; what he derived from me is immortal.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Hercules dwells in stars (after Jupiter takes him to heaven)
q: Jupiter enveloped him in a cloud, and took him up in a four-horse chariot to dwell among the stars.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Hebe is a goddess of youth
q: Hebe, the daughter of Juno, and goddess of youth, was cupbearer to the gods.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Hercules is subject to Eurystheus (by Juno's arts)
q: He was however by the arts of Juno rendered subject to his cousin Eurystheus and compelled to perform all his commands.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Hebe is daughter of Juno
q: Hebe, the daughter of Juno, and goddess of youth, was cupbearer to the gods.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Hebe is married to Hercules (after his apotheosis)
q: Juno, now reconciled to him, gave him her daughter Hebe in marriage.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Hebe is cupbearer to gods (before her office was given to Ganymede)
q: Hebe, the daughter of Juno, and goddess of youth, was cupbearer to the gods.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Ganymede is a Trojan boy
q: Her successor was Ganymede, a Trojan boy whom Jupiter, in the disguise of an eagle, seized and carried off from the midst of his playfellows on Mount Ida, bore up to heaven, and installed in the vacant place.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Ganymede succeeds Her successor (installed in the vacant place)
q: Her successor was Ganymede, a Trojan boy whom Jupiter, in the disguise of an eagle, seized and carried off from the midst of his playfellows on Mount Ida, bore up to heaven, and installed in the vacant place.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Jupiter assumes eagle form of Jupiter (to carry off Ganymede)
q: Her successor was Ganymede, a Trojan boy whom Jupiter, in the disguise of an eagle, seized and carried off from the midst of his playfellows on Mount Ida, bore up to heaven, and installed in the vacant place.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Hebe and Ganymede is a sculptural group (by Crawford)
q: But there is another statement which our countryman Crawford, the sculptor, has adopted in his group of Hebe and Ganymede, now in the gallery of the Boston Athenaeum.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Hebe and Ganymede is located in Boston Athenaeum (in its gallery)
q: But there is another statement which our countryman Crawford, the sculptor, has adopted in his group of Hebe and Ganymede, now in the gallery of the Boston Athenaeum.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Hercules performs twelve Labors of Hercules
q: Eurystheus enjoined upon him a succession of desperate adventures, which are called the twelve "Labors of Hercules."

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Juno is hostile to Hercules (because he was the offspring of Jupiter by a mortal mother)
q: As Juno was always hostile to the offspring of her husband by mortal mothers, she declared war against Hercules from his birth.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: twelve Labors of Hercules includes Nemean lion (as the first labor)
q: The first was the fight with the Nemean lion.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Nemean lion infests Nemea
q: The valley of Nemea was infested by a terrible lion.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Theseus is son of Aegeus (king of Athens)
q: Theseus was the son of AEgeus, king of Athens, and of Aethra, daughter of the king of Troezene.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Theseus abandons Ariadne (at Naxos)
q: On their way they stopped at the island of Naxos, where Theseus abandoned Ariadne, leaving her asleep.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Theseus is husband of Hippolyta (queen of the Amazons)
q: The queen of the Amazons whom Theseus espoused is by some called Hippolyta.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Theseus is husband of Phaedra
q: After the death of Antiope, Theseus married Phaedra, daughter of Minos, king of Crete.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Theseus is father of Hippolytus
q: Phaedra saw in Hippolytus, the son of Theseus, a youth endowed with all the graces and virtues of his father, and of an age corresponding to her own.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Theseus is slain by Lycomedes (treacherously)
q: Theseus at length lost the favor of his people, and retired to the court of Lycomedes, king of Scyros, who at first received him kindly, but afterwards treacherously slew him.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Theseus is honored by Theseum (after his death)
q: In a later age the Athenian general Cimon discovered the place where his remains were laid, and caused them to be removed to Athens, where they were deposited in a temple called the Theseum, erected in honor of the hero.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Theseus unites Attica (its several tribes into one state)
q: It is recorded of him that he united the several tribes by whom the territory of Attica was then possessed into one state, of which Athens was the capital.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Theseus institutes Panathenaea (in honor of Minerva)
q: In commemoration of this important event, he instituted the festival of Panathenaea, in honor of Minerva, the patron deity of Athens.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Athens is capital of Attica
q: It is recorded of him that he united the several tribes by whom the territory of Attica was then possessed into one state, of which Athens was the capital.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Athens pays tribute to Minos (seven youths and seven maidens every year)
q: The Athenians were at that time in deep affliction, on account of the tribute which they were forced to pay to Minos, king of Crete.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Theseus is son of Aegeus
q: Theseus was the son of AEgeus, king of Athens, and of Aethra, daughter of the king of Troezene.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Minos is king of Crete
q: The Athenians were at that time in deep affliction, on account of the tribute which they were forced to pay to Minos, king of Crete.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Crete is ruled by Minos
q: The Athenians were at that time in deep affliction, on account of the tribute which they were forced to pay to Minos, king of Crete.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Minotaur is a monster (with a bull's body and a human head)
q: This tribute consisted of seven youths and seven maidens, who were sent every year to be devoured by the Minotaur, a monster with a bull's body and a human head.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Minotaur is confined in the labyrinth
q: It was exceedingly strong and fierce, and was kept in a labyrinth constructed by Daedalus, so artfully contrived that whoever was enclosed in it could by no means find his way out unassisted.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Daedalus is a artificer (most skilful)
q: The labyrinth from which Theseus escaped by means of the clew of Ariadne, was built by Daedalus, a most skilful artificer.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Daedalus builds the labyrinth (for Minos)
q: Daedalus built the labyrinth for King Minos, but afterwards lost the favor of the king, and was shut up in a tower.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Daedalus is father of Icarus
q: So he set to work to fabricate wings for himself and his young son Icarus.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Daedalus invents saw
q: Imitating it, he took a piece of iron and notched it on the edge, and thus invented the SAW.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Daedalus invents pair of compasses
q: He put two pieces of iron together, connecting them at one end with a rivet, and sharpening the other ends, and made a PAIR OF COMPASSES.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Theseus is son of Aethra
q: Theseus was the son of AEgeus, king of Athens, and of Aethra, daughter of the king of Troezene.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: the labyrinth is built by Daedalus (for King Minos)
q: Daedalus built the labyrinth for King Minos, but afterwards lost the favor of the king, and was shut up in a tower.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: the labyrinth contains Minotaur (as its captive inhabitant)
q: It was exceedingly strong and fierce, and was kept in a labyrinth constructed by Daedalus, so artfully contrived that whoever was enclosed in it could by no means find his way out unassisted.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Ariadne is daughter of Minos
q: When they arrived in Crete, the youths and maidens were exhibited before Minos; and Ariadne, the daughter of the king, being present, became deeply enamored of Theseus, by whom her love was readily returned.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Ariadne loves Theseus (deeply; her love is returned)
q: Ariadne, the daughter of the king, being present, became deeply enamored of Theseus, by whom her love was readily returned.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Ariadne gives Theseus (a sword and a clew of thread)
q: She furnished him with a sword, with which to encounter the Minotaur, and with a clew of thread by which he might find his way out of the labyrinth.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Amazons are led by Antiope (as queen)
q: He assailed them before they had recovered from the attack of Hercules, and carried off their queen, Antiope.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Amazons are defeated by Theseus (in a battle fought in Athens)
q: The Amazons in their turn invaded the country of Athens and penetrated into the city itself; and the final battle in which Theseus overcame them was fought in the very midst of the city.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Pirithous is friend of Theseus (true brothers in arms)
q: Their deeds corresponded to their professions, and they ever continued true brothers in arms.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Pirithous descends into Tartarus (with Theseus)
q: Pirithous aspired to the wife of the monarch of Erebus; and Theseus, though aware of the danger, accompanied the ambitious lover in his descent to the underworld.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Icarus is son of Daedalus (young son)
q: So he set to work to fabricate wings for himself and his young son Icarus.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Theseus is successor of Aegeus
q: Theseus was acknowledged by his father, and declared his successor.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Icarus is submerged in the blue waters of the sea
q: While his mouth uttered cries to his father, it was submerged in the blue waters of the sea, which thenceforth was called by his name.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Castor and Pollux are children of Leda (born from an egg)
q: Castor and Pollux were the offspring of Leda and the Swan, under which disguise Jupiter had concealed himself. Leda gave birth to an egg, from which sprang the twins.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Castor and Pollux are patron deities of seamen and voyagers (after the Argonautic expedition)
q: From this incident, Castor and Pollux came afterwards to be considered the patron deities of seamen and voyagers

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Castor and Pollux are called Dioscuri (sons of Jove)
q: They received divine honors under the name of Dioscuri (sons of Jove).

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Castor and Pollux become Gemini (according to one form of the story)
q: According to another form of the story, Jupiter rewarded the attachment of the brothers by placing them among the stars as Gemini, the Twins.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Castor and Pollux are brothers of Helen (twins; Helen is their sister)
q: Helen, so famous afterwards as the cause of the Trojan war, was their sister.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Castor and Pollux participate in Argonautic expedition (together)
q: They accompanied the Argonautic expedition.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Castor and Pollux are associated with Castor and Pollux (ship) (one of St. Paul's ships bore their name)
q: One of the ships in which St. Paul sailed was named the Castor and Pollux.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Theseus is king of Athens
q: Theseus thus became king of Athens.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Pythian games are held at Delphi (in its vicinity)
q: The Pythian games were celebrated in the vicinity of Delphi

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Isthmian games are held at Corinthian isthmus
q: the Isthmian on the Corinthian isthmus

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Theseus defeats Procrustes
q: Theseus served him as he had served others.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Theseus is friend of Pirithous (inviolable fidelity)
q: The friendship between Theseus and Pirithous was of a most intimate nature, yet it originated in the midst of arms.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Theseus carries off Helen (with the aid of Pirithous)
q: Theseus fixed his choice on Helen, then but a child, afterwards so celebrated as the cause of the Trojan war, and with the aid of his friend he carried her off.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Theseus takes as companion Ariadne
q: He was successful, slew the Minotaur, escaped from the labyrinth, and taking Ariadne as the companion of his way, with his rescued companions sailed for Athens.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Bacchus is son of Jupiter
q: Bacchus was the son of Jupiter and Semele.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Bacchus marries Ariadne (on Naxos)
q: Bacchus found her, consoled her and made her his wife as Minerva had prophesied to Theseus.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Ariadne is a daughter of King Minos
q: Ariadne, the daughter of King Minos

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Ariadne is deserted by Theseus (on Naxos)
q: was carried by him to the island of Naxos and was left there asleep, while Theseus pursued his way home without her.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Ariadne receives Ariadne's crown (as a marriage present from Bacchus)
q: As a marriage present he gave her a golden crown, enriched with gems

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Jupiter confirms it (with the irrevocable oath)
q: Jove gives his promise and confirms it with the irrevocable oath, attesting the river Styx, terrible to the gods themselves.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Jupiter is father of Bacchus
q: Bacchus was the son of Jupiter and Semele.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Juno is hostile to Semele (because of resentment)
q: Juno, to gratify her resentment against Semele, contrived a plan for her destruction.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Juno causes Bacchus's madness
q: but Juno struck him with madness, and drove him forth a wanderer through various parts of the earth.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Semele is a mortal
q: Her mortal frame could not endure the splendors of the immortal radiance.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Semele is consumed to ashes ashes
q: She was consumed to ashes.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Bacchus is son of Jupiter
q: Bacchus was the son of Jupiter and Semele.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Phrygia is location of Rhea (where she cures Bacchus)
q: In Phrygia the goddess Rhea cured him and taught him her religious rites

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: India is destination of Bacchus's expedition to India (an expedition lasting several years)
q: The most famous part of his wanderings is his expedition to India, which is said to have lasted several years.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Thebes is native city of Bacchus
q: As he approached his native city Thebes

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Pentheus is a king (of Thebes)
q: Pentheus the king, who had no respect for the new worship, forbade its rites to be performed.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Pentheus opposes worship of Bacchus (forbidding its rites in Thebes)
q: Pentheus the king, who had no respect for the new worship, forbade its rites to be performed.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Bacchus is son of Semele
q: Bacchus was the son of Jupiter and Semele.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Pentheus is wounded by the whole band
q: The whole band rushed upon him, and while he now talks less arrogantly, now excuses himself, and now confesses his crime and implores pardon, they press upon and wound him.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Eteocles refuses to surrender the kingdom (to Polynices after his year of rule)
q: The first year fell to the lot of Eteocles, who, when his time expired, refused to surrender the kingdom to his brother.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Achelous loves Dejanira (as a suitor)
q: Perhaps you have heard of the fame of Dejanira, the fairest of maidens, whom a host of suitors strove to win. Hercules and myself were of the number

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Polynices is the brother of Eteocles
q: Her brothers, Eteocles and Polynices, had agreed to share the kingdom between them, and reign alternately year by year.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Polynices marries the daughter of Adrastus
q: Polynices fled to Adrastus, king of Argos, who gave him his daughter in marriage

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: the Seven against Thebes is a expedition (against Thebes)
q: This led to the celebrated expedition of the "Seven against Thebes," which furnished ample materials for the epic and tragic poets of Greece.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Creon is a king (of Thebes after the deaths of Eteocles and Polynices)
q: Creon, the uncle of the fallen princes, now become king

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Creon forbids the burial of Polynices (on pain of death)
q: Creon, the uncle of the fallen princes, now become king, caused Eteocles to be buried with distinguished honor, but suffered the body of Polynices to lie where it fell, forbidding every one, on pain of death, to give it burial.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Antigone's burial of Polynices exemplifies filial and sisterly fidelity
q: Antigone was as bright an example of filial and sisterly fidelity as was Alcestis of connubial devotion.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Penelope is a daughter of Icarius (a Spartan prince)
q: She was the daughter of Icarius, a Spartan prince.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Penelope marries Ulysses (king of Ithaca)
q: Ulysses, king of Ithaca, sought her in marriage, and won her over all competitors.
